excerpt: Compare Masaar and Al Zahia villas for family living by inspecting the home, school and work routes, community costs and ownership documents.
introduction:
Masaar and Al Zahia offer different Sharjah family settings. A villa in either community should be judged by its exact phase, layout, condition, daily journeys and full cost. A woodland plan or a nearby mall can be attractive, but neither guarantees the right home for every household.

Use the developer descriptions as starting points, then visit the property and check the facilities, ownership position and current terms for the specific villa.
takeaways: Compare the actual villa and phase, including usable rooms, parking, maintenance and outdoor space.
Test school and work journeys at the times your family will travel.
Verify ownership eligibility, community charges and the complete purchase and running costs.

sections.heading: What is different about the settings?
sections.body:
[Arada describes Masaar](https://www.arada.com/en/masaar/) as a community of villas and townhouses arranged around a green spine in Al Suyoh. [Al Zahia's community site](https://www.alzahia.ae/en) describes neighbourhoods with apartments, townhouses and villas and access to City Centre Al Zahia. These are developer descriptions, not proof that every facility is open or included for a particular home.

Check the exact phase and street, distance to the facilities you will use, parking and any ongoing construction. Ask which parts are operating now and what is still planned. A woodland view or mall access should be verified from the actual villa and route.

The [Sharjah family area guide](/journal/best-areas-to-buy-property-in-sharjah-for-families) provides a broader shortlist if other settings may also fit your family.

sections.heading: Inspect the villa and plot
sections.body:
Check bedroom placement, bathrooms, kitchen, storage, laundry and stairs. Consider the needs of children or older relatives and measure rooms for existing furniture. Inspect the garden, boundary, gate, drainage and allocated parking. Ask which appliances and fixtures are included.

Test cooling, water pressure, doors and windows where safe and permitted. Look for visible leaks or cracks, request maintenance records and obtain a qualified inspection for significant defects. If the villa has an extension or alteration, verify approvals and whether it matches the property records.

For an off-plan home, review the signed specification, plan, payment dates and handover terms. A show villa may not have the same layout or finish as the unit in the contract.

sections.heading: Test school and work journeys
sections.body:
List the actual school, nursery, workplace and healthcare destinations. Ask schools about admission, fees and transport for the exact address. Test the route at departure and return times, including school pickup. Test the commute from the entrance you would use at your usual travel times.

Check what happens if a car is unavailable and whether a second vehicle or school bus is needed. Visit on a working day and in the evening to assess access, noise and the household routine. Record the time and conditions rather than relying on an advertised drive time.

If a facility or road is planned, check its current status with the provider. Make sure the family can manage if delivery changes.

sections.heading: Compare all costs and ownership
sections.body:
Add the purchase price, buyer-paid registration and brokerage, lender fees, inspection and initial work. Request the current community charge, what it covers and any arrears. Include cooling, garden upkeep, insurance, school transport and commuting in an annual household budget. Keep a separate reserve for unexpected repairs.

Ask Sharjah's registration department to confirm the right available to your nationality for the exact villa. The [Sharjah ownership guide](/journal/how-to-check-foreign-ownership-eligibility-in-sharjah) explains how to check project approval, title and transfer. Review any mortgage, tenancy or developer clearance and obtain an itemised current quote.

If financing, compare the actual bank offer and payment calendar. A property should remain affordable after the down payment as well as on the day of purchase.

sections.heading: Use a family decision scorecard
sections.body:
Set non-negotiables for bedrooms, budget, legal eligibility and a workable school route. Score the remaining villas on evidence from the viewing. The chart shows one sample set of weights: layout and condition 35 points, travel 30, affordability 25 and community facilities 10. It does not rate Masaar or Al Zahia.

Mark unresolved questions, such as a school place or community charge, rather than treating them as favourable. Revisit the villa or seek documents before finalising a choice. The most suitable setting is the one that works for the household's actual routine and reserve.

chart.title: Example family villa priorities
chart.note: Sample weights total 100 points and do not score either community.

sections.heading: Check the community rules
sections.body:
Ask about visitor access, maintenance, permitted exterior changes, pets and the process for reporting a shared-area fault. If a clubhouse or pool matters, verify who can use it and whether a separate fee applies. A facility in the wider masterplan is not necessarily included in every villa's terms.

Request the management contact and any available charge history or information about planned work. Keep the documents with your comparison so the family's expectations match the obligations attached to the home.

Walk from the villa to the spaces your family expects to use and check crossings, lighting and access with children or a pushchair. Ask how residents are notified about maintenance or temporary closures. These practical details can differ between phases even when the community name is the same.

sections.heading: Request current villa options
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) and ask which specific Masaar or Al Zahia homes are currently available. [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, bedrooms and school and work destinations. Keep a comparison sheet for each villa you view.

Request the exact address, plan, price, community charges and ownership documents, then verify official requirements before committing.
